text: The sun—the star that converts nuclear‑potential energy into light, heat, and other forms of energy—was first accepted as the centre of the solar system in **1543**, when Nicolaus Copernicus published *De Revolutionibus Orbium Coelestium* (On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres). The book formally announced the heliocentric model, placing the sun at the heart of the planetary system and, for the first time, overturning the long‑held geocentric view that had prevailed since antiquity.
